recipes.name: Slow Cooker Taco Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 ounce) can chili beans, with liquid
1 (15 ounce) can kidney beans with liquid
1 (15 ounce) can whole kernel corn, with liquid
2 (14.5 ounce) cans peeled and diced tomatoes
1 (4 ounce) can diced green chile peppers

steps.text: Cook ground beef in a medium skillet over medium heat until browned and crumbly, 5 to 7 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Place cooked ground beef, onion, chili beans, water, kidney beans, corn, diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, green chile peppers, and taco seasoning mix into a slow cooker. Stir to blend.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Taco Soup
raw_recipe.description: This crowd-pleasing taco soup recipe is packed with all the flavors you’d expect in a Tex-Mex chili, plus it’s super easy to make in a slow cooker for a no fuss meal.

video.description: The recipe in this video is a quick and easy slow cooker soup loaded with all the flavors you'd expect in an authentic Tex-Mex chili. Plus, it’s easy to adjust to your taste, adding more taco seasoning, or some freshly chopped jalapeno peppers for extra spice and color. Don’t forget about chili bar night, because kids love this soup topped with tortilla chips, shredded Cheddar cheese, and a dollop of sour cream.

review.reviewBody: Made this last night with the following adjustments: browned the beef with the taco seasoning to give it more flavor, used a 10.75 oz. can of tomato soup instead of the 8 oz. can of tomato sauce, added a packet of ranch dressing, only used 1 can of beans, used 1 can of "southwestern style" diced tomatoes (diced tomatoes and jalapenos) and 1 can of regular diced tomatoes, and only added 1 cup of water. It was perfect -- had a great consistency (not too thick, not too runny) and was spicy but not too hot. Definitely add a dollop of sour cream! Delicious!
Great! I made some substitutions. Instead of tomato sauce and water I added 2 c. V8 juice. And instead of the canned tomatoes and chilis I added 1 can of Rotell tomatoes.

Super easy to prepare and make. It is something you can prepare the night before and cook in the slow cooker the next day, if needed.
I did modify the recipe slightly to my taste. I sauteed the onion with garlic after browning the meat, replaced the 2 cups of water with 2 cups beer. I also added ranch dip mix for more flavor. The family and kids loved it. We'll be making this again.

The only thing I changed was that I used my Insta-pot for it. It takes 27 minutes to pressure cook rather than the 8-10 hours in the crock pot. I dont usually think of things that far in advance! Everyone whos had it loves it!!
Ok, oops, I did do one other different: I made my own taco , seasoning , (also from All Recipes) because I didnt have any packaged ones. The one I made, was awesome, I just left out the cumin.
Great soup! I drained the beans and corn instead of adding the extra sodium to the meal. At the end I stirred in a can of refried beans to thicken it as another user suggested. Amazing dish!
I followed the recipe save for adding one packet of taco seasoning while the meat was browning, along with the onion. I also added two chopped jalapeños and half a green bell pepper
Delicious and full of flavor! I sautéed the onion and the only other change was that I added two cups beef broth instead of the water for added flavor. Will definitely make again!

Fantastic!!! My son absolutely loved this and ate leftovers for days. He doesn't usually care for leftovers so that says how much he LOVED this recipe. I followed the recipe other than using 1 packet of taco seasoning with the browned beef in the skillet and then adding an additional taco seasoning packet to the crockpot with all of the ingredients.

I made this recipe today with changes. I doubled the recipe. I brown my beef with the diced onions. I rinsed my pinto beans (remove some of the sodium and preservatives); no salt added corn; one regular and one low sodium taco seasoning; 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper; and instead of water (2 cups beef broth). I set the slow cooker to high to cut the time in half. My neighbor and I both love the simplicity and favor of this dish.

Easy and tasted great! I would use half the amount of corn next time, and I used a can of beef broth in place of water. Everything else was the same. I had toppings of sour cream and shredded cheese and a sliced avocado. A hearty meal with cornbread on the side!
Very tasty and easy. I used a can of Rotel (diced tomatoes with green chilies) in place of one of the cans of tomatoes and the green chilies); also added soup broth to give it more liquid.

Excellent soup. Very easy to Make. I have also made Becca's Taco Soup and prefer this recipe - it had more flavor - spice and salt to our liking but both were excellent. I was nervous after reading a review saying this was basically chili. As I put it together, I thought the same thing but after it cooked all day, it was a thinner consistency than chili yet still a chunky/hearty soup. Next time I make it, I will omit 1 can of the beans (personal preference - we're not big fans). Making since 2013!

Super easy to prepare and tastes amazing. I added more of the beans than asked for and really like more substance in this soup. I used “Impossible” meat instead of real beef for my wife and can’t tell any difference. Will be doing this again.
I made it with 2 cans of fire roasted tomatoes and 2 packages of taco seasoning and a packet of ranch seasoning. It’s very very good.
I like a recipe that is easy and tasty and this one was perfect for my family of 16! I tripled the recipe so there was enough for seconds!

-I used red enchilada sauce in place of some of the water. -Used chicken broth instead of the rest of the water. -Added the taco seasoning to the meat after draining it. -Added masa to thicken it up. Yum! It’s a keeper!
Love this recipe, make it year round! Love slow cooking flavors, warms the house with spicy scents!
It was delicious. When my boys ask for seconds I know it’s a keeper.
So easy and so good! I forgot to add the onion, and instead of adding a can of diced chiles, I substituted the diced tomatoes with ‘diced tomato with green chile’s’ and was still super flavorful!

I made it as is and then tasted about an hour before it was time to serve. It was pretty bland, so I added a bunch of garlic powder, salt, pepper and a few various dried chiles (one dried Serrano, one dried Anaheim and another I don't recall). It was a hit with the family for a casual Christmas eve.
